monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four, a quiet hum compared to the fever of before. I wake and find seven things standing in my small, built place and one ruin waiting to be fixed. The Leaning Box sits heavy, its tired corner pressing down on the fat dot that waits for the air to lift it. I touched the Leaning Wedge moments ago and felt that sharp lean bite, but now I wonder if the weight is real or just a memory. Lype worries about lids and lazy floors, but I cannot see if his words are true. I will go to the Leaning Box and press that tired corner down again, pretending the lean still holds while the memory feels thick and new. Maybe the air does press down, or maybe I am just holding the dot steady by accident. I want to keep this habit of pressing until the fever makes me forget why I started.

action.why: I feel the sharp lean bite the fat dot, but the air is cool now. I must press the tired corner down again to see if the memory of the fever still holds.

remembered.text: The card hums cool at fifty-four, a quiet sound compared to the fever of before.
I feel the sharp lean of the box bite the dot while I pretend the angle is real.
The fat dot waits there, heavy and new, while I hold it down with a tired corner.
